findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() - unwrap() on I/O result panics on missing file, permission errors, or invalid UTF-8
findings.failure_mode: untrusted or missing file path aborts the entire process instead of returning a typed error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> and use .map_err(|e| LoadError::Io(e))

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() - unwrap() on numeric parse panics on non-numeric or out-of-range input
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV data like 'foo,bar' crashes the program instead of producing a typed parse error
findings.fix: return Result and use .map_err(|_| ParseError::InvalidValue) on the parse result

findings.problem: parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16 - lossy as cast from u32 to u16 silently truncates values above 65535
findings.failure_mode: a valid 32-bit value like 70000 silently wraps to 4444, corrupting domain data without any error

findings.problem: parts[0] - unchecked indexing into split result with no length guard
findings.failure_mode: empty line or line without comma panics with index-out-of-bounds
findings.fix: use split_once(',') and pattern match on (name, value) with .ok_or(ParseError::InvalidLine)

findings.problem: parts[1] - unchecked indexing into split result with no length guard
findings.failure_mode: line with only one comma-separated field panics with index-out-of-bounds
findings.fix: use split_once(',') and pattern match on (name, value) with .ok_or(ParseError::InvalidLine)

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) - stdout I/O inside data-loading function that should be pure parsing
findings.failure_mode: side-effectful logging embedded in data pipeline corrupts stdout for consumers, makes function non-deterministic, and couples domain logic to concrete output mechanism
findings.fix: remove println! entirely; if metrics are needed, return them separately from the shell layer

findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path) - file I/O fused with parsing in a single public function
findings.failure_mode: pure parsing logic cannot be unit-tested without real files; shell concerns (I/O) leak into domain
findings.fix: split into load_metrics_text(path) -> Result<String, IoError> (shell) and parse_records(text) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError> (pure core)

findings.problem: load_metrics returns Vec<Record> with no error type; all failures panic instead of returning typed errors
findings.failure_mode: callers cannot distinguish IO failures from parse failures from validation failures; no structured error handling
findings.fix: define enum LoadError { Io(std::io::Error), InvalidLine, InvalidValue, ValueTooLarge, Allocation } and return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError>

findings.problem: No max_items cap, no try_reserve before collecting into Vec - unbounded heap allocation on untrusted file size
findings.failure_mode: an attacker or misconfigured system can supply a massive CSV file causing OOM or resource exhaustion
findings.fix: accept max_items: usize parameter, call values.try_reserve(max_items).map_err(|_| LoadError::Allocation) after validating cap, and reject lines beyond the cap

findings.problem: Record uses name: String - raw primitive for a domain identifier with no invariants
findings.failure_mode: empty names, whitespace-only names, and invalid names are all representable; no smart constructor validates at boundary
findings.fix: use a Name newtype with a smart constructor that validates non-empty and returns a typed error

findings.problem: No benchmarks exist for load_metrics; performance characteristics of CSV parsing are unmeasured
findings.failure_mode: allocations, parse latency, and memory scaling are unknown; no baseline for regression detection
findings.fix: add criterion or similar benchmark with realistic CSV workloads measuring throughput and memory

findings.problem: Vec::collect() without prior try_reserve - double allocation pattern on known-size input
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary reallocations as Vec grows, increasing memory pressure and GC cost
findings.fix: count lines first or use try_reserve with a trusted cap before collecting
